issues.legal_issue: A transfer requiring registration is not complete for the purpose of a statutory right of reconveyance until registration is completed, even if the transferee’s title may relate back to the date of execution.
material_facts: A sale deed was executed and presented for registration, but registration was completed only after the applicant lodged the reconveyance application.
The applicant relied on the rule that, once registration occurred, the transferee’s title related back to the date of execution.
issues.conclusion: The transfer was completed only when registration was completed; the relation-back effect did not make the transfer complete on the date the deed was executed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 16(2)(iii) and 16(3) of the Bihar Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling Area and Acquisition of Surplus Land) Act, a transfer requiring registration is not complete before registration. Section 47 of the Registration Act does not alter that result. The Court followed Ram Saran Lal v. Mst. Domini Kuer, Radhakishan L. Toshniwal v. Shridhar, and Bishan Singh v. Khazan Singh.

predicates.statutory_reconveyance_proceeding: A person seeks a statutory right to have land conveyed back following a transfer to another person.
predicates.transfer_requires_registration: The transfer can take effect only through a registered instrument.
predicates.registration_not_completed: The registration process for the instrument has not been completed.

issues.definition: When a statutory reconveyance proceeding concerns a transfer requiring registration, the transfer is not complete while registration remains unfinished.

issues.legal_issue: A Collector may entertain a reconveyance application lodged before registration is complete if the transfer is complete by the time the Collector first considers the application.
material_facts: The applicant delivered the application to the Collector’s office before registration was completed, and a subordinate later endorsed it for placement before the Collector.
The Collector first considered the application on the day registration was completed and then acted on it.
The Collector’s receipt of the application, or a subordinate’s endorsement, did not amount to the Collector entertaining it.
issues.conclusion: The Collector had jurisdiction to entertain the application because the transfer was complete when the Collector first considered it; earlier delivery to the office did not mean that the Collector had already entertained it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(3) of the Bihar Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling Area and Acquisition of Surplus Land) Act makes a completed transfer a prerequisite to the Collector’s jurisdiction. The Court applied the principles in Ram Saran Lal v. Mst. Domini Kuer, Radhakishan L. Toshniwal v. Shridhar, and Bishan Singh v. Khazan Singh as to when a transfer and the resulting right are complete.

predicates.statutory_reconveyance_proceeding: A person seeks a statutory right to have land conveyed back following a transfer to another person.
predicates.application_lodged_before_transfer_compl: The applicant delivered the application to the relevant office before the transfer was complete.
predicates.transfer_complete_when_collector_conside: The transfer was complete when the Collector first considered the application.
predicates.collector_may_entertain_application: The Collector is permitted to take up and decide the application.

issues.definition: If an application is lodged before the transfer is complete but the transfer is complete when the Collector first considers it, the Collector may entertain the application.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to attach a copy of the registered deed does not invalidate a reconveyance application when the attachment requirement is directory and the applicant supplies the information needed for the Collector to proceed.
material_facts: The applicant deposited the purchase price and an additional ten per cent and attached the deposit challan.
The applicant claimed as a co-sharer and sought reconveyance on the terms of the sale deed.

Because registration had not yet been completed when the application was lodged, the applicant attached an accurate certified copy of the sale deed tendered for registration rather than a copy of the registered deed.
The Collector had the information needed to consider the application when it was placed before him after registration was completed.
issues.conclusion: The omission of a copy of the registered deed was not fatal and did not deprive the Collector of jurisdiction; the certified copy supplied was sufficient because it provided the necessary information.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(3) of the Bihar Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling Area and Acquisition of Surplus Land) Act requires the qualifying applicant to make the prescribed deposit and provides for reconveyance. Rule 19 of the Bihar Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling Area and Acquisition of Surplus Land) Rules, 1963 prescribes filing a copy of the registered deed, but does not specify that non-compliance invalidates the application. Whether a procedural requirement is mandatory or directory depends on the enactment’s scope and object. The deposit, the applicant’s qualifying status and readiness to accept reconveyance on the sale terms, and a completed transfer are conditions precedent; the deed-copy requirement is directory because its object is to inform the Collector. The Court relied on Buland Sugar Co. v. Municipal Board, and applied Bellamy v. Saull and King v. Lincolnshire Appeal Tribunal; Ex parte Stubbins.

predicates.statutory_reconveyance_proceeding: A person seeks a statutory right to have land conveyed back following a transfer to another person.
predicates.transfer_complete_when_collector_conside: The transfer was complete when the Collector first considered the application.
predicates.qualifying_claimant: The applicant belongs to a class entitled to seek reconveyance under the applicable scheme.
predicates.required_deposit_made: The applicant deposited the required purchase price and additional sum.
predicates.applicant_willing_to_accept_sale_terms: The applicant offered to accept reconveyance on the terms and conditions of the sale.
predicates.accurate_sale_deed_copy_supplied: The applicant attached an accurate copy of the deed tendered for registration.
predicates.registered_copy_unavailable: A copy of the registered deed was unavailable to the applicant when the application was filed because registration had not been completed.
predicates.collector_has_necessary_information: The materials before the Collector provided the information needed to consider the transfer, its terms, and the required deposit.

issues.definition: When a qualifying applicant has made the required deposit, is willing to accept the sale terms, and supplies an accurate deed copy that gives the Collector the necessary information while a registered copy is unavailable, the missing registered copy does not invalidate the application.
